mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2% does not lead to tighter monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points over the past month signals a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE decrease does not correlate with improved corporate earnings.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the past two months signals increased economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with increased economic activity.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4% signals a restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS > 4% does not lead to a restrictive monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past two months signals a weakening supply side, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decrease does not correlate with a weakening supply side.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over the past month signals increased consumer spending, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS increase does not correlate with increased consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points over the past month, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.3pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combined increase in PAYEMS and decrease in UNRATE does not correlate with improved corporate earnings.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% annualized over the past two months, it signals inflationary pressure with a tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of high FEDFUNDS and increasing CPIAUCSL does not lead to negative returns.
